rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: You Owe Me a Miracle
card.instruction: Carry one past favor as sufficient reason to expect an impossible act in return, and present the exchange as perfectly fair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I covered your lunch yesterday. Bring back the ten minutes I spent queuing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy your lunch today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That covers the sandwich. I'm only asking for my time back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can queue for you today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. Use that time to retrieve yesterday's minutes. Then we're square.

card.title: You Owe Me a Miracle
card.instruction: Carry one past favor as sufficient reason to expect an impossible act in return, and present the exchange as perfectly fair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I helped move your sofa. Move the moon away from my window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those aren't equivalent favours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sofa had stairs. The moon's already airborne.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll move your bed away from the window. I have twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then move the moon for twenty minutes each night. I didn't leave your sofa halfway upstairs.

card.title: Effortlessly Unbelievable
card.instruction: Be sincerely impressed by how naturally someone inhabits the strange reality, then compete to appear even less surprised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asked that talking doorway for directions without hesitating. That's impressive. I usually just chat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then ask it where the toilets are. We're late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Morning, door. Usual question: toilets?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Upstairs. It wants a tooth; I usually give a baby tooth.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A molar, door. Keep the change. You still count out baby teeth?

card.title: Effortlessly Unbelievable
card.instruction: Be sincerely impressed by how naturally someone inhabits the strange reality, then compete to appear even less surprised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You greet invisible guests so easily. I wish I had your touch. Actually, I usually hug them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the umbrella stand. Martin's behind you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Martin! No formalities between us. Come for supper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I usually ask whether he can eat visible food first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, we can skip all that. Martin, help yourself from the fridge whenever. I'll get you a key.

card.title: Don’t Let Reality Notice
card.instruction: Behave as though openly questioning the impossible premise could attract dangerous attention, and respond to doubt with urgent normality.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call Mum's floating chair impossible. Reality might hear. Pass her the potatoes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's above the table. I can't reach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just a high chair. Fetch the stepladder; dinner's getting cold.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's at the ceiling now. I'm calling for help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Call it room service. Ask for a taller ladder and three desserts upstairs. We're having a perfectly ordinary family dinner.

card.title: Don’t Let Reality Notice
card.instruction: Behave as though openly questioning the impossible premise could attract dangerous attention, and respond to doubt with urgent normality.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lower your voice about the singing moon. We don't want it noticing us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everybody can hear it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then call it weather. Weather gets away with anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's singing my name. Should I answer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only with 'Lovely evening.' Keep walking. We're just two people discussing the forecast.

transfer.action: I lay the old lunch-money receipt beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: You said anything. I've saved the word. {request}
transfer.response: I consider that modest interest on a long-ago kindness. {counter}
transfer.closing: A promise of anything should expect ambitious collection.

transfer.action: I address the talking wall beside {prop} with practised nonchalance.
transfer.opening: Only a talking wall. How ordinary. {request}
transfer.response: Some of us have always spoken fluent brick. {counter}
transfer.closing: By how much fuss people make about an entirely routine impossibility.

transfer.action: I cover {prop} and whisper toward the floating chairs.
transfer.opening: Don't let reality hear the word impossible. {request}
transfer.response: Say it as though chairs have always done that. {counter}
transfer.closing: Not at that volume. We're trying to keep the arrangement unnoticed.
